# Changelog

All notable changes to the Bitcoin Research Kit (BRK) project will be documented in this file.

> *This changelog was generated by Claude Code*

## [v0.12.0](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/releases/tag/v0.12.0) - 2026-08-28

### Breaking Changes

#### Workspace, `bitviewd`, and deployment

- Recast BRK as a reusable Bitcoin data foundation and moved the ready-to-run application into the Bitview layer. The former monolithic application crates now have focused `bitview_*` counterparts for composition, computation, querying, serving, clients, MCP, code generation, types, and the website; embedders can assemble only the layers and plugins they need ([architecture](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview/src/lib.rs))
- Narrowed the `brk` umbrella crate to reusable Bitcoin primitives. Its `full` feature no longer includes the former bencher, bindgen, client, cohort, computer, indexer, query, server, or traversable layers; those APIs now live in Bitview crates, and Bitview-specific schema types such as series data, search, pagination, health, and sync status moved from `brk_types` to `bitview_types` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk/Cargo.toml), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_types/src/lib.rs))
- Renamed the daemon from `brk` to `bitviewd`, moved its default data directory from `~/.brk` to `~/.bitview`, replaced `--brkdir` with `--bitviewdir`, replaced `--brkport` with `--serverport`, and added `--serverbind`. Configuration now lives at `~/.bitview/config.toml`, and the REST server defaults to `0.0.0.0:3110` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd/src/config.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd/src/main.rs))
- Removed automatic REST port scanning. `bitviewd` now acquires the exact configured socket before background work begins and exits when that address is unavailable, making deployment failures immediate and predictable ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd/src/main.rs))
- Changed the default data layout to `<bitviewdir>/plugins/<plugin-id>`. The active plugin composition owns that complete `plugins` directory and deletes entries that are not claimed by the composition; operators who run different plugin sets must give each set a separate Bitview directory. Each plugin also owns its root schema and resets only its own incompatible data ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/src/storage.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime/src/plugin_set.rs))
- Did not migrate or reuse the former `~/.brk` database layout. Existing operators must plan a fresh import in `~/.bitview` or an explicitly selected Bitview directory ([architecture](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md))
- Increased the current default composition's documented on-disk requirement to about 290 GiB at the indexed tip, excluding Bitcoin Core, filesystem overhead, chain growth, and reimport headroom. Because VecDB uses sparse files, operators should measure allocated space with `du -sh ~/.bitview` instead of Finder or `ls` logical sizes ([architecture](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md))
- Renamed the Docker image, container, user, volume, executable, and data paths around Bitview. The compose example maps host port `7070` to the daemon's container port `3110` and persists `/home/bitview/.bitview` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/docker/docker-compose.yml), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/docker/Dockerfile))

#### `bitview_client`, generated packages, and public types

- Renamed the Rust crate, JavaScript package, Python package, and primary client class from the `brk_client`/`brk-client`/`BrkClient` family to `bitview_client`/`bitview-client`/`BitviewClient`. Imports and construction code must use the new names ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_client/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/modules/bitview-client/index.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/packages/bitview_client/bitview_client/__init__.py))
- Split native script classification from Esplora-compatible naming. `OutputType` now distinguishes and serializes `p2pk65`, `p2pk33`, `p2pkh`, `p2ms`, `p2sh`, `opreturn`, `p2wpkh`, `p2wsh`, `p2tr`, `p2a`, `empty`, and `unknown`, while `OutputTypeNormalized` supplies Esplora values such as `p2pk`, `multisig`, `op_return`, `v0_p2wpkh`, `v0_p2wsh`, `v1_p2tr`, and `anchor`; consumers matching the former serialized values must migrate ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/output_type.rs))
- Changed dates in the public schema from their internal integer representation to `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, documented every serialized transaction-output field with Esplora-normalized script types and an optional address, and corrected transaction-input requirements so witness and inner-script assembly remain optional while `prevout` remains present as a nullable value. Generated clients now reflect the actual transaction wire shapes ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/date.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/txout.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/txin.rs))
- Corrected fixed and lossless public schemas: reward and fee totals serialized as decimal strings are now typed as strings; mempool fee histograms are arrays of two-item pairs; difficulty-adjustment entries are fixed four-number tuples; and fixed-bin histograms carry exact minimum and maximum lengths. Regenerated clients no longer infer lossy numbers, object maps, or variable-length arrays for those responses ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/reward_stats.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/mempool_info.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/difficulty_adjustment_entry.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/histogram.rs))
- Narrowed `Weight` to the 32-bit range required by a single block or transaction and added `Weight64` for accumulated totals. Rust consumers that stored aggregate weights in `Weight` must use the new wide type even though JSON remains numeric ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/weight.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/weight64.rs))

#### `bitview_query`, `bitview_server`, and API consumers

- Rebuilt the generated series tree around metric-first columnar sources, changing many public series identifiers and typed access paths rather than merely relocating their implementation. Unsuffixed value-destroyed rolling series now split into explicit `_cents` and `_usd` names; cohort matrices expose typed `..._by_class`, `..._by_epoch`, `..._by_type`, and `..._by_term` sources; and the former `addrs.indexes` plus `addrs.data` raw groups are replaced by `addrs.state`, whose per-script primary records are joined by `funded` and `extendedEmpty` sidecars. Consumers with hard-coded identifiers must use v0.12 discovery or regenerate their client instead of assuming every v0.11 path remains an alias ([v0.11.2 client](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/modules/brk-client/index.js), [v0.12.0 client](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/modules/bitview-client/index.js))
- Changed the existing structured error body's media type from `application/json` to `application/problem+json`, retaining the `{ "error": { "type", "code", "message", "doc_url" } }` shape. Requests made while plugin state is changing now receive retryable `503 Service Unavailable` responses with `Retry-After: 1` instead of observing mixed snapshots ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/error.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/lib.rs))

#### `bitview_mcp`

- Renamed the MCP binary and crate from `brk_mcp` to `bitview_mcp`. Its command line now requires all three named options: `--api` for the upstream REST origin or bare host, `--url` for the public MCP origin, and `--name` for discovery metadata. It rejects positional, unknown, duplicate, empty-name, path-bearing, query-bearing, credential-bearing, and non-HTTP(S) origins; the former single positional API-origin invocation no longer applies ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/arguments.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/config.rs))

#### BRK foundation and storage APIs

- Replaced `brk_reader::Reader`'s raw crossbeam-channel return values with `BlockReceiver`, a named blocking stream that implements `Iterator` and also offers borrowed `.iter()`. Code that named or manipulated the former `Receiver<Result<ReadBlock>>` type must adopt the wrapper ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_reader/src/block_receiver.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_reader/src/lib.rs))
- Narrowed `brk_error::Result` from `Result<T, E = brk_error::Error>` to `Result<T>`, and made the equivalent `rawdb::Result` and `vecdb::Result` aliases single-error aliases too. Callers that supplied a custom error parameter must use `std::result::Result<T, E>` directly; each crate alias now consistently means that crate's own error ([BRK source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_error/src/lib.rs), [RawDB source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/rawdb/src/error.rs), [VecDB source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/error/mod.rs))
- Changed `brk_logger::register_hook` callbacks from formatted `&str` messages to borrowed `tracing::Event` values. Hook users can now inspect targets and typed structured fields, but must record or format the event themselves instead of receiving a preformatted string ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_logger/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_logger/src/hook.rs))
- Replaced `brk_oracle`'s `HistogramRaw`, `HistogramEma`, and `HistogramEmaCompact` type aliases with distinct transparent newtypes. Direct consumers must unwrap through `Deref` or use the new zeroing, increment, accumulation, division, and compact-projection methods; the separation prevents raw counts, smoothed floats, and wire-quantized bins from being mixed accidentally ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_oracle/src/histogram_raw.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_oracle/src/histogram_ema.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_oracle/src/histogram_ema_compact.rs))
- Simplified the published `brk_byteview` surface to immutable `ByteView` ownership. `StrView`, public mutation through `Mutator`/`get_mut`, zero-filled `with_size`, detached cloning, explicit refcount access, and several convenience conversions were removed; construction now goes through immutable values or the hidden builder used by storage internals ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/byteview/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/byteview/src/byteview.rs))
- Changed `brk_store::Store` construction and commit ownership: the public `Mode` and `StoreMeta` surfaces are gone; `Store::import` no longer accepts a mode; `import_cached` and manual cache clearing are gone; and `take_pending_ingest` no longer takes a height or persists metadata itself. It returns a `PendingIngest` for the caller to execute before explicitly persisting the database, so direct users must update their durability sequence ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_store/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_store/src/pending_ingest.rs))
- Changed several direct `vecdb` APIs as storage ownership became explicit. `ReadableBoxedVec` and `CachedBoxedVec` are named cloneable wrappers instead of bare boxed-trait aliases; cached snapshots now return `Arc<Vec<T>>`, `cached()` became `snapshot()`, and `clear()` became `invalidate()`; raw-vector hole and replacement mutation moved behind `MutableVec`; unchecked deletion helpers are gone; and the public iterator-writer implementation became an internal detail. Direct library users must construct the wrappers, use the mutable facade, and adopt the snapshot/invalidation accessors ([readable source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/traits/readable_boxed.rs), [cached source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/cached/cloneable.rs), [mutable source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/mutable/mod.rs), [writer source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/traits/any_with_writer.rs))
- Removed `rawdb::Database::set_min_regions`; database size now follows actual region allocation instead of preallocating an arbitrary region count. Related regions can be registered through the new `RegionGroup` API when they need to keep a shared relative layout during relocation ([database source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/rawdb/src/lib.rs), [group source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/rawdb/src/region_group/mod.rs))
- Replaced `vecdb`'s safe `Pco`/`TransparentPco` marker pair and the public `AsInnerSlice`, `AsInnerSliceMut`, and `FromInnerSlice` casting helpers with one unsafe `Pco` conversion contract. Manual implementations must now provide `to_number` and fallible `from_number`, and may set `IS_TRANSPARENT` only when the value and PCO number have identical layouts and valid bit patterns; `#[derive(Pco)]` generates that contract for transparent one-field wrappers ([trait source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/compressed/pco/trait.rs), [strategy source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/compressed/pco/strategy.rs), [derive source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb_derive/src/lib.rs))
- Changed mining-pool address matching to accept a parsed `AddrBytes` payload instead of a string and to use a prebuilt address-to-pool map. Direct `Pools::find_from_addr` callers must parse the address first; repeated block attribution no longer scans every configured pool address ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/pools.rs))

### New Features

#### `bitview_plugin`, `bitview_runtime`, and `bitview_default`

- Added a first-class plugin contract built around `PluginId`, `PluginStorage`, `ImportContext`, and typed `ComputePlugin::Dependencies` and `ComputePlugin::Output` associations. A plugin now has one identity, one schema root, one finalized database set, explicit dependencies, and lifecycle-only update context rather than reaching into a global computer ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/src/storage.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/src/compute_plugin.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/src/update_context.rs))
- Marked the new platform and plugin APIs experimental while the built-in modules are being extracted. External plugin authors should expect compatibility changes despite the runnable typed example and persisted plugin identity contract ([guide](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/README.md), [guide](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd/README.md))
- Added `PluginSet` derivation with nested-set flattening, field skipping, duplicate-ID rejection, typed traversal, and an explicit compute schedule. Custom compositions can therefore preserve compile-time dependencies while controlling which plugins are stored, queried, and executed ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime_derive/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime/src/plugin_set.rs))
- Added whole-update read gating. Every plugin gate closes before mutation, safe cursors are committed before gates reopen, failures leave all gates closed, and multi-plugin guards acquire locks without retaining a partial set; API readers see either the previous committed state or the next one, never an in-between graph ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/src/gate.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/src/read_guard.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime/src/update.rs))
- Added bootstrap decisions that can request a reimport after plugin initialization and again after catch-up. In release builds, when the node is more than 10,000 blocks behind, the default runtime announces a ten-second delay, imports only the indexer, releases its temporary state, reimports the graph from the new persisted cursor, and then computes the complete graph before the server becomes available ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime/src/bootstrap.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_default/src/compute.rs))
- Parallelized independent parts of the default graph while preserving an explicit dependency schedule: mappings and blocks establish the base; inputs and prices run together; market, outputs, and the transactions-to-mining/OP_RETURN branch run together; investing follows; pools run beside distribution; indicators and Capital Sentiment run beside the supply-to-Cointime branch and Coinflow; Bedrock and Rarity Meter finish after their sources exist ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_default/src/import.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_default/src/compute.rs))
- Added a process-lifetime `bitview` runner for embedding the default composition and left `bitviewd` as a small command-line shell around it ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd/src/main.rs))
- Added a complete custom-plugin example. `near_full_block_streak` records consecutive blocks at or above 90% of maximum block weight, persists and rolls back safely, declares typed dependencies, joins the default composition, and appears through the generic series API without hand-written query or server routes ([guide](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/examples/custom_plugin/README.md), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/examples/custom_plugin/src/near_full_blocks/compute.rs))

#### Distribution and cohort analytics

- Expanded complete distribution families to calendar-year cohorts from 2009 through 2026 and halving epochs 0 through 4. Each receives supply in profit/loss, delta and dominance shares, UTXO and spent-output counts, realized capitalization and price, realized profit/loss/net, unrealized profit/loss/net, NUPL, MVRV, transfer volume, value and coindays destroyed, and 24-hour SOPR where the underlying inputs apply ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/cohorts.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/mod.rs))
- Exposed the same analytical surface across 23 age buckets from less than one hour through more than 15 years, cumulative under/over thresholds through 15 years, and address-balance bands. Address-balance cohorts additionally report address and UTXO counts, supply, realized capitalization and P/L, and transfer volume ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/cohorts.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/columnar/mod.rs))
- Converted the existing script/address-type cohort family to independently readable columnar sources and exposed its raw matrices alongside the individual projections. Output, prevout, and transaction-with-type counts remain comparable with supply, UTXOs, spent outputs, realized and unrealized values, profitability, and activity without storing a separate row wrapper for every script type ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_cohort/src/by_addr_type.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/columnar/rows/mod.rs))
- Converted the existing address-reuse, respending, and exposed-public-key families to shared per-address-type column stores while retaining active and all-time address counts, input/output event counts, held supply, and relative shares. Reuse still means funded more than once; public-key exposure still covers P2PK and P2TR funding and hash-based scripts after their witness or script reveals the key, with P2A excluded ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/addr/reused/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/addr/exposed/mod.rs))
- Standardized profitability composition across aggregate and columnar cohorts: supply and invested capital in profit or loss, their shares, unrealized P/L relative to cohort market capitalization, gross P/L composition, realized gross P/L and peak regret, one-month net-P/L change relative to realized and market capitalization, and pain, greed, and net sentiment now share common sources and definitions ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/columnar/amount_value.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/columnar/cumulative/value_with_amount_and_type.rs))
- Reworked the existing 25 exact profitability buckets—from more than 1,000% in profit through 90–100% in loss—and their cumulative profit/loss thresholds into term-by-range column stores. All/STH/LTH slices retain individual supply, realized capitalization, absolute unrealized P/L, and NUPL series, while the raw matrices can be read as one typed source ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_cohort/src/profitability.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_cohort/src/profitability_range.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/profitability/vecs.rs))
- Extended existing all-chain behavioral metrics to matching STH/LTH aggregates where applicable, including coin-years destroyed, dormancy, extended-window SOPR, profit-to-loss ratio, sell-side risk, adjusted SOPR, transfer volume in profit and loss, and realized or unrealized values relative to Bitcoin or cohort market capitalization ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/activity/vecs/collection.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/realized/vecs/collection.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/metrics/relative/vecs.rs))
- The default composition now exposes 61,764 series, 3,742 more than v0.11.2, while retaining the same 97 REST operations. Most of the increase comes from applying existing analytical families consistently to the new year, halving, age, balance, and script/address-type cohorts ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_default/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_query/src/query_plugin_set.rs))

#### Blocks, transactions, OP_RETURN, prices, and models

- Added sum, cumulative sum, minimum, maximum, median, p10, p25, p75, p90, and average block-weight series, making weight distributions queryable instead of exposing only raw per-block values ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_blocks/src/weight/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_blocks/src/weight/import.rs))
- Made the existing OP_RETURN analytics independently selectable as a dedicated plugin and stored its 23 content-kind and four policy-class breakdowns as columnar matrices. Individual projections retain output and transaction counts, payload bytes, full carrier-transaction virtual size and fees, proportional shares, cumulative totals, and rolling windows, while raw breakdown rows can be read as one source ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_op_return/src/vecs/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_op_return/src/vecs/compute.rs))
- Added a 50-day price SMA, converted the existing EMA periods to one independently readable columnar source, and made price, market, supply, inputs, outputs, transactions, mining, pools, indicators, investing, Bedrock, Rarity Meter, Capital Sentiment, Cointime, and Coinflow independently selectable plugins ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_market/src/moving_average/sma.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_market/src/moving_average/import.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_default/src/lib.rs))
- Packed each Rarity Meter extreme's existing 0.1%, 0.05%, and 0.025% boundaries into a columnar height source while retaining named threshold projections, historical tail share, and discrete rank for coins in loss, profit taking, capitulation, peak regret, and seller exhaustion ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_rarity_meter/src/extreme.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_rarity_meter/src/threshold_vecs.rs))

#### `bitview_query` and `bitview_server`

- Made series discovery generic over a traversable plugin set. Feature and capability traits compile routes only for supported data, query handlers retain direct typed references instead of performing hot-path lookups, and a custom plugin's vectors become searchable and fetchable without server-specific registration ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_query/src/query_plugin_set.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_query/src/vecs/cohort_query.rs))
- Added human-readable descriptions, including documented formulas, to series metadata and search. Discovery now matches metric names, description terms, and cohort aliases, with deterministic typo-tolerant and partial-word ranking while preserving exact direct-path access ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_types/src/series_info.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_query/src/vecs.rs))
- Extended `quickmatch` with owned indexes, compact stable item IDs, matched-query-word counts, and a switch for disabling disjoint-word union fallback. Bitview uses those results to rank direct names, expanded cohort aliases, and descriptions together; replacing raw-pointer posting sets with owned-or-borrowed items also removes the matcher’s former manual `Send` and `Sync` assertions ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/quickmatch/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/quickmatch/src/config.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_query/src/vecs.rs))
- Extended the existing weak-ETag matcher to examine every repeated `If-None-Match` header field in addition to strong/weak values, wildcards, and comma-separated alternatives. Compression now uses the fastest setting only for responses of at least 1 KiB, and the five-second API timeout no longer cuts off large static website assets ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/etag.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/cache/params.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/lib.rs))
- Retained bounded response defaults across generated surfaces, including a 50 MB maximum response weight and a 1,000-item default UTXO limit, so newly generated clients and CLI commands do not silently request unbounded datasets ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/api/mod.rs))

#### `bitview_bindgen` and `bitview_cli`

- Added OpenAPI-driven CLI generation for every non-deprecated operation: positional path parameters, scalar and repeatable query flags, typed request bodies, per-command help, `--url`/`BITVIEW_URL`, and `--pretty`. The generated CLI defaults to `http://localhost:3110` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_cli/src/generated.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_cli/src/main.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_cli/src/request_body.rs))
- Extended bindgen with CLI targets, request-body schemas, structural pattern analysis, field-name and field-position reconstruction, and richer description propagation. The Rust, JavaScript, Python, CLI, MCP, OpenAPI, and LLM outputs are now derived from the same analyzed API structure ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_bindgen/src/generators/cli.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_bindgen/src/openapi/request_body.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_bindgen/src/analysis/positions.rs))

#### `bitview_mcp`

- Added a discovery website at `GET /` with privacy, terms, support, and logo routes while retaining the MCP transport on `POST /`. Discovery metadata now includes the configured public site, server name, title, and icon ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/page.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/server.rs))
- Replaced the fixed 50-requests-per-second gate with a 16-request concurrency limit that waits up to five seconds and reports retryable busy responses. Origin restrictions apply to state-carrying POST requests rather than public discovery pages, and upstream REST requests have a 15-second deadline ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/server.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/upstream.rs))
- Added a 32 KiB URL ceiling, an 8 MiB response ceiling, percent-encoded path parameters, scalar-array query parameters, binary responses as embedded MCP resources, and one-hour public caching metadata for discovery and tool catalogs. Bare API hosts retain the existing HTTPS-first fallback ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/config.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/server.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/upstream.rs))
- Curated the generated MCP catalog to favor bounded analytical operations: precise fee summaries, structured price data, sync state, search, lists, counts, versions, blocks, and transactions remain available, while health/docs helpers, raw block transfer, very large mempool payloads, redundant pages, and unbounded series-tree/data calls are omitted ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_mcp/src/manifest.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_bindgen/src/generators/llm/manifest.rs))

#### `vecdb`, `rawdb`, `brk_store`, `fjall`, and `lsm-tree`

- Added `ColumnarVec<V, C>` for values with exactly one varying axis. A logical row is stored as one independently readable contiguous column per axis value, with equal-length and stamp validation, atomic visibility, lazy column projections, and column sums; distribution cohorts use this to avoid duplicating row metadata while preserving independent compression and reads ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/columnar/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/columnar/column.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/columnar/sum.rs))
- Added `OverflowVec`, which keeps common compact values inline and stores uncommon full-width values in a reusable sidecar slot. It supports mutation, rollback, hole reuse, read-only access, and cursor traversal for metrics whose rare large values should not determine every row's width ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/overflow/vec.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/overflow/value.rs))
- Added mutable vector views, bounded raw and compressed range cursors, grouped raw-database regions, access-tracked region retention, compressed metadata caches, and a global decoded-source cache budget. Range reads now decode only the required spans and independent plugin columns can be paged without materializing their siblings ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/mutable/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/rawdb/src/region_group/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/compressed/inner/page.rs))
- Made RawDB flushes track and merge the actual dirty subranges, restore them after a failed mmap flush or file sync, and make data durable before synchronizing metadata that exposes it. Region relocation and hole punching now carry explicit pending state, while grouped regions move together and keep their relative layout, reducing needless writes without weakening crash recovery ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/rawdb/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/rawdb/src/region.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/rawdb/src/region_group/inner.rs))
- Added a narrowly scoped Pco fork whose `read_uninit` path decompresses directly into spare vector capacity, avoiding an initialization and copy pass for large pages while leaving the upstream format intact ([patch note](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/pco/BRK_PATCH.md), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/compressed/inner/decoder.rs))
- Reduced the existing BRK-owned `fjall` and `lsm-tree` forks to the table-only path required by `brk_store` bulk indexing. Strictly sorted in-memory batches become durable SSTables without a journal, public memtable, snapshot API, or cross-keyspace transactions; equal-key insertion order is preserved across sequential and mixed batches, fixed leveled compaction maintains the table set, and manifests and tables are synchronized before an ingestion finishes ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_store/src/lib.rs), [design](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/fjall/README.md), [design](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/lsm-tree/README.md))

#### Websites and experiments

- Rebuilt the classic website's cohort adapter around the generated metric-first Bitview series tree. Its typed projector derives all, term, age, UTXO-amount, address-balance, script-type, class, and entry-price views while omitting metrics that a selected cohort does not provide, replacing the former hand-shaped UTXO/address trees ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website/scripts/options/distribution/cohort-tree.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website/scripts/options/distribution/cohort-tree-types.d.ts), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website/scripts/options/distribution/data.js))
- Rewired the classic site's existing address exposure/reuse/respending, Cointime, Coinflow, OP_RETURN, and model charts to the Bitview metric-first paths, then extended the catalog for the broader cohort families, 50-day SMA, and block-weight statistics introduced by the new composition ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website/scripts/options/partial.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website/scripts/options/network.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website/scripts/options/network/op-return.js))
- Expanded `website_next` Explore with a live confirmed/projected chain cube, block-clock and interval state, direct height/hash navigation, smooth block transitions, reorganization recovery, scroll and orientation controls, a cached hover X-ray, a dedicated block X-ray pane, and richer header, miner, reward, and transaction previews ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website_next/explore/chain/index.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website_next/explore/block/xray/index.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website_next/explore/block/index.js))
- Added the `website_next_next` bento-style prototype covering Bitview, the reusable BRK foundation, API discovery, block-height exploration, and research experiments ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/tree/v0.12.0/website_next_next))
- Added an interactive BRK architecture and product story that explains the reusable foundation, Bitview plugin stack, data flow, local-first deployment, and API surface ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/experiments/brk/index.html))
- Added Finding the Floor, an interactive comparison of eight market-floor approaches spanning cost-basis percentile staircases, full/local/cycle Rarity Meter views, raw/Cointime/Coinflow Bedrock percentiles, URPD structure, and an extreme-event finder ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/experiments/floor/index.html))
- Added the HODL Wave explorer with supply, capital, Cointime, and Coinflow weighting, live age composition, normal and 100%-stacked views, date scrubbing, cohort isolation, and responsive controls ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/experiments/wave/index.html))
- Migrated the Bedrock, Rarity Meter, Extreme Events, Capital Sentiment, and Satoshi Trail experiments to the Bitview API and client names while preserving their live model views and shareable controls ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/tree/v0.12.0/experiments))
- Replaced the generic `brk_bencher` harness with `bitviewd_bench`, a one-shot instrumented run of the real default bootstrap schedule. It records production plugin timings, build/host/chain metadata, completion state, memory, I/O, physical disk growth, and indexed progress without deleting an existing database; the companion SVG visualizer overlays multiple runs with aligned progress cutoffs ([guide](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd_bench/README.md), [guide](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd_bench_visualizer/README.md))
- Published complete v0.12 benchmark traces and rendered comparisons for an M3 Pro using internal SSD storage and an M4 using a Thunderbolt 4 SSD, including production plugin timings, sampled memory and I/O, physical disk usage, and indexed-height progress ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/tree/v0.12.0/benches/bitviewd/v0.12_m3pro_int_ssd), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/tree/v0.12.0/benches/bitviewd/v0.12_m4_tb4_ssd))

### Bug Fixes

#### `brk_types`, `bitview_client`, and generated clients

- Fixed P2PK address-hash-prefix discovery by preserving the distinction between 33-byte compressed and 65-byte uncompressed public-key payloads. Both forms now produce the correct prefix and match behavior across generated Rust, JavaScript, and Python helpers ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/output_type.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_client/src/lib.rs))
- Fixed P2A/anchor script reporting by keeping the native `P2A` classification separate and emitting the expected normalized `anchor` value in Esplora-compatible responses ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/output_type.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/api/transactions.rs))
- Replaced floating-point internal fee rates with fixed `u64` millisatoshi-per-vbyte values, including an explicit non-finite sentinel, exact averaging and rounding, and checked conversions. External JSON remains decimal fee rates or `null`, but repeated aggregation no longer accumulates binary floating-point drift ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/feerate.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/feerate_percentiles.rs))
- Corrected the `/api/series/count` OpenAPI and generated-client response type from `Vec<SeriesCount>` to `DetailedSeriesCount`. The runtime already returned the detailed `{ total, by_db }` object, so regenerated clients now describe the established wire response instead of expecting an array ([v0.11.2 source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_server/src/api/series.rs), [v0.12.0 source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_server/src/api/series.rs))
- Corrected the generated Rust and Python clients' default base URL from the unused `http://localhost:3000` to Bitview's `http://localhost:3110`; callers that supplied an explicit origin are unaffected ([Rust generator](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_bindgen/src/generators/rust/client.rs), [Python generator](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_bindgen/src/generators/python/api.rs))
- Fixed typed-client construction of age-over and age-under transfer-volume paths when a suffix pattern contains a templated child. Rust, JavaScript, and Python clients now produce identifiers such as `utxos_over_10y_old_transfer_volume` instead of incorrectly placing `over` after `transfer_volume` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_bindgen/src/generate/fields.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/modules/bitview-client/index.js))

#### `bitview_runtime` and `bitview_server`

- Fixed update visibility so errors cannot reopen only part of the plugin graph or expose new vectors beside old dependent vectors; the read gate remains closed until the next successful full commit ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime/src/update.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin/src/gate.rs))
- Fixed API startup races by binding the configured address before long-running bootstrap work and publishing the server only after initial catch-up and any requested reimport complete ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd/src/main.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime/src/bootstrap.rs))

#### `website`

- Increased the classic chart renderer's common series width from 1 to 1.5 pixels while preserving the library's narrow literal type, making dense line charts easier to distinguish without a JavaScript type error ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/website/scripts/utils/chart/index.js))
- Replaced platform-dependent emoji event markers in Extreme Events with explicit filled and ring shapes, stable colors, and zoom-responsive sizing, preventing operating-system glyphs from changing the chart legend or obscuring candles ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/experiments/events/index.html))

### Internal Changes

#### BRK foundation crates

- Separated reusable node access into `brk_reader`, `brk_rpc`, `brk_mempool`, `brk_oracle`, `brk_store`, and `brk_types`. Typed batched RPC calls, a compact mempool-entry representation, streaming transaction-ID array parsing, consistent RPC errors, and block-template transaction types now serve both Bitview and independent consumers ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_rpc/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_rpc/src/rpc_client/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_mempool/src/lib.rs))
- Preserved structured tracing fields in console logs instead of flattening them into an ambiguous message: non-HTTP events render as `message — key=value`, HTTP access events retain their compact status/URI/latency form, and logger-private plus `internal.*` timing fields remain hidden. The event hook now lets `bitviewd_bench` consume those hidden typed timings without changing operator-facing logs ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_logger/src/format.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd_bench/src/benchmark/trace.rs))
- Replaced broad all-in-one compute/index/query ownership with focused plugin crates for constants, index data, mappings, blocks, price, market, inputs, outputs, transactions, mining, pools, supply, distribution, OP_RETURN, indicators, investing, Capital Sentiment, Cointime, Coinflow, Bedrock, and Rarity Meter. Each crate owns its state, schema, and typed dependency boundary ([architecture](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_default/src/lib.rs))
- Switched long-running Bitview processes to mimalloc and made decoded-vector cache allocation a shared runtime budget, allowing completed import stages and temporary sources to return memory before the next graph stage ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitviewd/src/main.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_runtime/src/bootstrap.rs))
- Replaced full per-address primary records with a four-byte tagged `AddrState`: common empty-address lifetime totals stay inline, larger empty records and funded records live in reusable `OverflowVec` sidecars, and common funded counters and realized capitalization use a compact 32-byte representation. This keeps the primary address arrays dense without losing exact large values or reorg-safe mutation ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/addr_state.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_distribution/src/addr/state_vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_types/src/funded_addr_data_compact.rs))
- Batched and parallelized high-volume compute paths without changing their metric definitions: transaction fees and same-block CPFP clusters run in 64-block batches, OP_RETURN carriers aggregate by block before writing, block byte/vbyte distributions run independently, URPD age ranges merge in parallel, address-state updates reuse typed buffers, and unchanged mempool projections are reused only when membership, block-template order, and minimum fee are all unchanged ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_transactions/src/fees/compute.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/bitview_plugin_op_return/src/vecs/batch/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/crates/brk_mempool/src/snapshot/rebuilder.rs))

#### Documentation and release tooling

- Rewrote architecture, daemon, client, CLI, MCP, plugin, custom-plugin, storage, Docker, and benchmark documentation around the Bitview composition model, destructive plugin-root ownership, exact bind behavior, fresh data layout, and generated interfaces ([architecture](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [documentation](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/tree/v0.12.0/docs))
- Reworked generation, publishing, and quick-release scripts for the expanded workspace so Rust crates, JavaScript/Python packages, API documentation, MCP manifests, and release tags are produced in dependency order and can resume safely after a partial release ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/scripts/quick-release.sh), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/scripts/rust-publish.sh))
- Changed the MIT license attribution from the former 2025 BRK-only notice to the 2026 Bitcoin Research Kit and Bitview project identity ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.12.0/LICENSE))

**Full Changelog**: [v0.11.2...v0.12.0](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/compare/v0.11.2...v0.12.0)

## [v0.11.2](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/releases/tag/v0.11.2) - 2026-08-08

### Breaking Changes

#### `brk_computer` and generated clients

- Changed the existing inscription, annex, SIGHASH, dust, CPFP parent/child, CoinJoin, consolidation, and batch-payout count leaves from direct per-block endpoints into `AverageBlockCumulativeSumPattern` objects. Callers that want the former series must insert `.block` before the index selector; `.cumulative`, `.sum`, and `.average` now expose the added aggregate forms ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/features/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/fees/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/patterns/vecs.rs))
- Moved nonstandard-transaction counts from `transactions.policy.count` to `transactions.policy.count.nonstandard` and expanded the value from a per-block-only series into per-block, cumulative, and rolling forms. Typed Rust, JavaScript, and Python paths now reflect the extra `nonstandard` level and the richer series shape ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/policy/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/modules/brk-client/index.js))

### New Features

#### `brk_indexer`, `brk_computer`, and transaction analytics

- Added per-block, cumulative, and rolling counts for transactions containing inscriptions, annexes, dust outputs, and each SIGHASH family: ALL, NONE, SINGLE, DEFAULT, and ANYONECANPAY. Each count measures transaction presence once, and a transaction may contribute to multiple feature families ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/features/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/features/compute.rs))
- Added total BIP141 signature-operation cost as per-block, cumulative, and rolling series under `transactions.sigops.total` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/sigops/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/sigops/compute.rs))
- Expanded confirmed CPFP parent/child, CoinJoin, consolidation, batch-payout, and nonstandard-policy counts from per-block values to matching cumulative and rolling series, making these transaction behaviors comparable over time without client-side aggregation ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/fees/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/patterns/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/policy/vecs.rs))
- Added a reusable block-index cumulative-sum computation that folds flat transaction segments into height-indexed totals and emits zero-valued blocks when no matching transaction occurs ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/internal/per_block/computed/cumulative_rolling.rs))

#### `website`

- Added transaction chart groups for confirmed CPFP parents and children, total sigop cost, five SIGHASH families, inscriptions, annexes, CoinJoin, consolidation, batch payout, dust, and nonstandard policy beside the existing count, TPS, volume, velocity, fee, size, and version views ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/website/scripts/options/network/transactions.js))
- Added a dedicated Sigop Cost display unit so BIP141 cost totals are not presented as raw transaction counts ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/website/scripts/utils/units.js))

#### Experiments

- Added Extreme Events, a live dashboard for Rarity Meter tails across profit taking, capitulation, peak regret, seller exhaustion, and coins in loss. It displays 1%, 0.5%, 0.25%, 0.1%, 0.05%, and 0.025% thresholds, historical markers, one-second price polling, and 60-second series refreshes ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/experiments/events/index.html))
- Added Capital Sentiment, a live view of score, phase, long/short state, price candles, all/STH/LTH capitalized prices, and the one-year price SMA. Spot-to-capitalized-price relationships define the phase structure, while the SMA confirms or disambiguates transitions ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/experiments/sentiment/index.html))
- Expanded Satoshi Trail with 1-week, 1-month, 3-month, 6-month, 1-year, 2-year, and 4-year comparison modes; signed terrain above and below zero; water palettes and caps; profile loading; revised age cohorts; stronger mobile/landscape behavior; hover detail; and cached data reuse ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/experiments/trail/index.html))
- Renamed the Rarity experiment from “Bitcoin Rarity Model” to “Bitcoin Rarity Meter” and made the BRK attribution in Bedrock, Rarity Meter, and Satoshi Trail link to the project site instead of rendering as inert text ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/experiments/rarity/index.html), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/experiments/bedrock/index.html), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/experiments/trail/index.html))

#### Generated clients

- Exposed the complete transaction-feature, sigop, pattern, CPFP, and policy tree through generated Rust, JavaScript, and Python clients, including cumulative and rolling accessors for every newly aggregated count ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_client/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/modules/brk-client/index.js))
- Increased the published metric catalog from 57,886 to 58,022 series while retaining 97 REST operations, reflecting the aggregate transaction paths added in this release ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/website/llms.txt))

### Bug Fixes

#### `vecdb`

- Fixed sparse lazy aggregation at a partially filled final group by clamping the group's end boundary to the source length. Queries can now aggregate a source whose last range is incomplete without reading past its final value ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/vecdb/src/variants/lazy/agg/sparse.rs))

### Internal Changes

#### `brk_indexer` and `brk_computer`

- Connected the transaction feature flags already produced by the indexer to dedicated computer import and vector modules, keeping decoding in the indexer while centralizing height aggregation in the computer ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_indexer/src/vecs/transactions/features/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/features/import.rs))
- Hid the indexer's eight raw feature-count vectors from traversal after the computer gained aggregate wrappers, preventing duplicate public paths while leaving the per-transaction feature flags queryable ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_indexer/src/vecs/transactions/features/schema.rs))
- Reused the same cumulative-and-rolling construction across feature, sigop, pattern, fee, and policy families, including empty-block handling and common rolling windows ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.2/crates/brk_computer/src/internal/per_block/computed/cumulative_rolling.rs))

**Full Changelog**: [v0.11.1...v0.11.2](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/compare/v0.11.1...v0.11.2)

## [v0.11.1](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/releases/tag/v0.11.1) - 2026-08-06

### Breaking Changes

#### `brk_computer`, generated clients, and `website`

- Changed the lowest Rarity Meter percentile from `pct0_01` (0.01%) to `pct0_1` (0.1%) across stored components, model output, Rust/JavaScript/Python client paths, website labels, and chart colors. The model storage schema advances accordingly, so callers and stored data using `pct0_01` must migrate ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/crates/brk_computer/src/models/rarity_meter/components.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/crates/brk_computer/src/models/rarity_meter/inner.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/website/scripts/options/models/rarity-meter.js))

### New Features

#### Address indexing

- Added reusable block-address loading and parallel cache preparation for large blocks. When at least 128 distinct address-backed outputs or inputs are touched, the indexer preloads them with Rayon; non-address script types are skipped, and smaller blocks retain the lower-overhead sequential path ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/crates/brk_computer/src/distribution/block/cache/addr.rs))
- Added block-source tracking so cached address state can distinguish records loaded from persistent storage from addresses first allocated in the block being processed ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/crates/brk_computer/src/distribution/block/cache/addr.rs))

#### Experiments

- Added Bedrock, an interactive model explorer for raw, Cointime, and Coinflow cost-basis views; technical and art presentations; logarithmic and linear scales; P95, P98, P99, P99.5, and P99.9 loss thresholds; L10 through L90 floor bands; and live API data ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/experiments/bedrock/index.html))
- Added a Rarity Meter explorer for full-history, local, and cycle scopes with percentile bands, rainbow and candlestick presentations, selectable query/local storage, and shareable state ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/experiments/rarity/index.html))
- Added Satoshi Trail, a canvas terrain view of URPD and cost-basis distributions with cohort, metric, aggregation, raw/Cointime/Coinflow weighting, camera angle, persistent settings, shareable URLs, concurrent fetching, and response caching ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/experiments/trail/index.html))

#### Release tooling

- Made quick releases resumable when the requested workspace version and its Git tag already exist. A resumed run skips rebuilding, regenerating documentation, bumping versions, and recreating the tag, then reruns the registry publication steps, whose publishers skip artifacts that already exist ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/scripts/quick-release.sh))
- Routed Rust publication through workspace-aware `cargo-release` ordering, including `brk_website`'s generated or dirty working state, already-published crates, pipeline error propagation, temporary logs, and separate pacing for new versus existing packages ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/scripts/rust-publish.sh), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/scripts/release.sh))

### Bug Fixes

#### Address indexing

- Fixed current-block address allocations being skipped solely because the flush-interval cache already contained their type index. Any address at or beyond the block's first newly allocated index is now seeded from fresh default state before block processing; older addresses still load their funded or empty state from storage ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/crates/brk_computer/src/distribution/block/cache/addr.rs))

#### Generated clients

- Replaced stale `0.3.6` metadata with the `0.11.0` API/client-generation baseline in the JavaScript and Python packages and in both websites' compact/full LLM references. The regenerated Rust, JavaScript, and Python trees also expose the renamed 0.1% Rarity Meter path consistently ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/modules/brk-client/package.json), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/packages/brk_client/pyproject.toml), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/website/llms.txt))

### Internal Changes

#### Rarity Meter and website presentation

- Kept the revised lowest percentile synchronized across persisted component naming, model assembly, generated path traversal, labels, and color definitions so there is one public interpretation of the tail threshold ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/crates/brk_computer/src/models/rarity_meter/components.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/website/scripts/utils/colors.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.1/website/scripts/options/shared.js))

**Full Changelog**: [v0.11.0...v0.11.1](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/compare/v0.11.0...v0.11.1)

## [v0.11.0](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/releases/tag/v0.11.0) - 2026-08-05

### Breaking Changes

#### `brk_types`, `brk_computer`, and generated clients

- Replaced most basis-point values with parts-per-million storage and API types. `BasisPoints16` and `BasisPointsSigned16` were removed, the 32-bit types became `PartsPerMillion32` and `PartsPerMillionSigned32`, and new signed and unsigned 64-bit variants were added. Generated Rust, JavaScript, and Python series paths consequently use `.ppm` instead of `.bps`, including renamed metrics such as `block_fullness_ppm` and `price_sma_200d_ratio_ppm` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/parts_per_million_32.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/parts_per_million_64.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/parts_per_million_signed_64.rs))
- Reserved the maximum integer encodings of `Cents` and `CentsCompact` as `NAN` sentinels. `MAX` now denotes that sentinel, finite callers must use `MAX_FINITE`, and direct integer extraction from a sentinel now fails instead of treating it as a price ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/cents.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/cents_compact.rs))
- Renamed the serialized `SeriesCount` fields from `distinct_series`, `total_endpoints`, `lazy_endpoints`, and `stored_endpoints` to the shorter `distinct`, `total`, `lazy`, and `stored` names ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/series_count.rs))
- Reorganized and reduced the exported metric tree to remove redundant stored cohort variants and duplicated realized-price SMA, deviation, z-score, and band families. OP_RETURN metrics moved from `scripts.raw.op_return` into the dedicated top-level `op_return` tree. Consumers should regenerate typed clients and review removed or relocated paths before upgrading stored data ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/distribution/metrics/config.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/lib.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/op_return/vecs.rs))
- Reorganized entry-price cohorts under the semantic `cohorts.utxo.entry.discount` and `cohorts.utxo.entry.premium` paths, while retaining the stored Veteran and Rookie series prefixes for existing data ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/distribution/vecs.rs))
- Split the broad `6m-1y` and `1y-2y` UTXO age cohorts into `6m-9m`, `9m-1y`, `1y-18m`, and `18m-2y`, and added matching under/over 9-month and 18-month aggregates. Series keyed by the former ranges must migrate to the new cohort paths ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_cohort/src/age_range.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_cohort/src/under_age.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_cohort/src/over_age.rs))

#### `vecdb` and `brk_traversable`

- Replaced `LazyVecFrom1` with the general single-source `LazyVec` and removed `LazyVecFrom2` and `LazyVecFrom3`. Multi-source arithmetic is now performed explicitly through eager or binary transform operations, keeping lazy vector derivations tied to one source ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/vecdb/src/variants/lazy/vec/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/vecdb/src/ops/binary_transform/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_traversable/src/lib.rs))

#### `quickmatch`

- Changed result ordering to rank matches by matched-word count, fuzzy score, earliest match position, candidate length, and deterministic lexical order. Applications that depended on the previous result order should treat the new order as part of the matching upgrade ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/quickmatch/src/lib.rs))

### New Features

#### `brk_mcp`

- Added `brk_mcp`, a thin, stateless, read-only MCP adapter generated from BRK's OpenAPI document. Every tool invocation is forwarded as a `GET` request to the configured REST origin, allowing deployments to reuse the REST API's Cloudflare cache without adding response caching or session state to the MCP server ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_mcp/src/server.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_mcp/src/upstream.rs))
- Added a single-argument `brk_mcp <REST_API_URL_OR_HOST>` interface. Bare hosts try HTTPS first and fall back to HTTP only after a transport failure; explicit origins are used as supplied. The local Streamable HTTP server starts at `127.0.0.1:3111` and tries successive ports through `3211` when occupied ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_mcp/src/config.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_mcp/src/main.rs))
- Embedded the generated tool manifest in the binary at compile time and added request-size, concurrency, rate, and Origin protections around the public MCP endpoint. This release implements MCP protocol version `2026-07-28`; the official stateless, tokenless instance is available at `https://mcp.bitview.space/` ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_mcp/generated/manifest.json), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_mcp/src/manifest.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_mcp/README.md))

#### `brk_bindgen` and clients

- Added OpenAPI-driven MCP manifest generation and compact/full LLM documentation generation so the MCP tool catalog, `llms.txt`, and `llms-full.txt` share the canonical REST API descriptions instead of maintaining a separate hand-written API surface ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_bindgen/src/generators/llm/manifest.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_bindgen/src/generators/llm/mod.rs))
- Added RapidHash v3 address-payload prefix and match helpers to the generated Rust, JavaScript, and Python clients, plus mainnet Bitcoin address decoding and address-string hashing in Rust. Public clients can discover address candidates without sending a raw address or xpub to the server ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_bindgen/src/generators/rust/client.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_bindgen/src/generators/javascript/client.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_bindgen/src/generators/python/client.rs))
- Added per-request `memCache` control to generated JavaScript endpoint methods, independently of their HTTP/browser `cache` option, so callers can bypass the parsed-response LRU for selected requests ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_bindgen/src/generators/javascript/api.rs))
- Expanded generated endpoint metadata and parameter descriptions for both API readers and agents, including exact address-hash behavior, URPD weighting, endpoint cache policy, and typed request/response schemas ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_bindgen/src/openapi/endpoint.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_server/src/api/openapi/mod.rs))

#### `brk_indexer`, `brk_computer`, and `brk_types`

- Added raw OP_RETURN indexing and 23 protocol/content classifications: Runes, VeriBlock, Omni, Stacks, Blockstack, Colu, OpenAssets, Komodo, CoinSpark, Poet, Docproof, OpenTimestamps, Factom, EternityWall, Memo, Bitproof, Ascribe, Stampery, Epobc, BareHash, Text, Empty, and Unknown ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/op_return_kind.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_indexer/src/processor/txout/op_return.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_indexer/src/vecs/op_return.rs))
- Added total, per-kind, and policy OP_RETURN metrics for output and transaction counts, data bytes, virtual size, fees, chain share, data share, fee share, cumulative totals, and rolling windows ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/op_return/vecs.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/op_return/by_kind.rs))
- Added transaction analysis for scriptSig, redeem scripts, witnesses, output scripts, sighash modes, sigops, annexes, inscriptions, fake public keys and script hashes, dust, and nonstandard-policy conditions. The resulting typed flags and counts are stored per transaction for queries and downstream metrics ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_indexer/src/processor/transaction/analysis/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_indexer/src/processor/transaction/analysis/policy.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_indexer/src/vecs/transactions/features/mod.rs))
- Added CoinJoin, consolidation, and batch-payout transaction-pattern series together with nonstandard-transaction policy metrics ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/patterns/compute.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/patterns/coinjoin.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/policy/compute.rs))
- Added confirmed same-block CPFP cluster construction with ancestor and descendant relationships, chunk linearization, effective fee rates, sigops-adjusted virtual sizes, per-transaction parent/child flags, and per-block parent/child counts, extending CPFP analysis beyond the live mempool ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_query/src/impl/cpfp/confirmed.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/transactions/fees/vecs.rs))

#### Frameworks and models

- Added the Coinflow framework with spending rate, exposure, mobility, mobile and immobile supply, all/STH/LTH splits, 1-month through 8-year horizons, capitalization, price, and loss-share series ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/frameworks/coinflow/compute.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/frameworks/coinflow/vecs.rs))
- Made Cointime canonical under the new `frameworks.cointime` tree while retaining the legacy top-level `cointime` branch, and expanded it with age-range coindays created, consumed, and stored; wakefulness and dormancy; awake and dormant supply; all/STH/LTH aggregates; adjusted capitalization and prices; reserve risk; and loss-share series ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/frameworks/mod.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/frameworks/cointime/age_range/compute.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/frameworks/cointime/aggregate/compute.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/frameworks/cointime/supply/vecs.rs))
- Added the Bedrock model with raw, cointime, coinflow, and horizon-weighted URPDs; P95, P98, P99, P99.5, and P99.9 loss thresholds; floor percentiles; and L10 through L90 price levels ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/models/bedrock/compute.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/models/bedrock/vecs.rs))
- Added the Capital Sentiment model with ten named phases, a score, and long/short state derived from spot price, capitalized-price references, and the one-year price moving average ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/capital_sentiment_phase.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/models/capital_sentiment/compute.rs))
- Moved Rarity Meter from indicators into the models tree and expanded it with full-history, local, and cycle variants; percentile components; rank and tail thresholds; and extreme-state metrics for coins in loss, profit taking, capitulation, peak regret, and seller exhaustion ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/models/rarity_meter/components.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/models/rarity_meter/extremes.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/models/rarity_meter/percentiles.rs))

#### URPD

- Added `raw`, `cointime`, and `coinflow` URPD weighting for latest, dated, and discovery queries. Responses now identify their selected weight, and weighted aggregate distributions are persisted for model and API reuse ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/urpd_weight.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_query/src/impl/urpd.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_server/src/api/urpd.rs))

#### Mining pools

- Added DMND as mining-pool ID 171, removed fixed pool-count assumptions, added pool JSON ID/slug validation, and exposed each block's ordinal `block_number` among blocks attributed to its pool. The pool catalog can now grow without changing array constants in consumers ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/pools-v2.json), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/pools.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_types/src/block_pool.rs), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/crates/brk_computer/src/pools/pool_heights.rs))

#### `website_next`

- Added Bitview Ask, an entirely browser-side assistant using the approximately 580 MB Bonsai 4B model through WebGPU. Model files and conversations stay in the browser, with streaming responses, multiple chats, conversation compaction, stop/copy/remove controls, Markdown rendering, inline charts, and timing details ([source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/website_next/ask/model.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/website_next/ask/worker.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/website_next/ask/storage.js), [source](https://github.com/bitcoinresearchkit/brk/blob/v0.11.0/website_next/ask/conversation/index.js))
